belongs_to: Lilavati problem (Bhaskaracharya): lotus in a lake whose tip is 1 unit above the water and touches the water 3 units away; worked solution 3^2 + x^2 = (x+1)^2, depth x = 4
description: Coloured illustration of a pond seen from the side, placed to the right of the problem text. A wide pale green-grey rectangle of water (rounded, soft edges) with a lighter water-surface line near its top; the lake bed is a dark green-grey strip along the bottom edge with weed tufts (about 3 tufts on the left, 2 on the right) that are decoration. Centre: one lotus (pink flower) on a straight, thick, dark vertical stem that stands upright from a point on the lake bed at bottom centre, up through the water surface, to the flower above the water. Two double-headed dimension arrows lie along this stem: an upper arrow from the water surface up to the flower base, labelled "1" (to its right); and a lower arrow from the water surface straight down to the lake bed, labelled "x" (to its right, in italics). Left: a second pink lotus flower sitting exactly at the water surface (the swayed position, tip touching the water). A straight thick dark line runs diagonally from this left flower down-right to the foot of the vertical stem on the lake bed (this is the swayed stem, the hypotenuse of length x + 1; it carries no label). A thin horizontal line runs along the water surface from the left flower to the vertical stem (the 3-unit distance; it carries NO label, the number 3 is not printed in the picture). So the figure shows a right triangle with vertical side x (depth), horizontal side along the surface, and the diagonal stem as hypotenuse; the right angle is at the point where the horizontal surface line meets the vertical stem. Right of the stem: a green frog sitting on a dark lily pad at the surface, plus a second dark lily pad further right (decoration only). The only printed labels are "1" and "x".
unclear: A very small tick/mark at the right end of the horizontal surface line, next to the stem, may be a tiny right-angle mark; too small to be sure
The horizontal segment carries no '3' in the picture although the text says 3 units

belongs_to: Figure it Out Q8 (Math Talk / Try This): "(i) Using the dots of a grid as the vertices, can you create a square that has an area of (a) 2 sq. units, (b) 3 sq. units, (c) 4 sq. units and (d) 5 sq. unit? (ii) Suppose the grid extends indefinitely..."
description: Square dot grid printed to the right of Q8 (left of the Math Talk and Try This badges). 5 columns by 5 rows of black solid dots = 25 dots (counted), equally spaced; grey grid lines run through the dots: 5 horizontal and 5 vertical lines, so the dots mark the corners of a 4 x 4 block of 16 unit cells (each cell a square of side 1 unit). The grid lines extend a short stub beyond the outermost dots on all four sides. No axes, numbers, letters, shading or marked squares - it is an empty grid for the student to draw squares on.
unclear: The book does not state the grid unit; unit cell = 1 unit is implied by the question (areas in sq. units)
